title: Crisis Helpline Responder (Australia)
description:
Are you passionate about making a difference for those in urgent need? As a Crisis Helpline Responder, you’ll provide immediate support and guidance to individuals in crisis, offering compassionate listening, crisis intervention, and critical referral services to help callers navigate their most challenging moments.
In this role, you’ll work closely with a dedicated team of mental health professionals, ensuring the safety and well-being of callers by connecting them with the appropriate resources and support systems.
This flexible, remote part-time role allows you to work from anywhere. While we prefer local candidates fluent in the local language, we welcome all qualified applicants aligned with our mission.
Why This Role Matters
Your role is essential in providing a lifeline to individuals experiencing distress, including those affected by suicide, self-harm, or mental health crises. You’ll be trained in evidence-based techniques to deliver immediate relief and guide callers to the appropriate resources, making a tangible impact in people’s lives.
Responsibilities

• Responding to telephone hotline for crisis support of those bereaved through suicide, engaging in self-harm, experiencing suicide ideation and concerned friends or family members.

• Conducting over the phone risk assessments and high risk assessment, including but not limited to, lethality assessment for suicide cases or individuals who have been found to be at risk.

• Providing a range of evidenced based, professional crisis counseling services and personal support, employing de-escalation techniques and crisis intervention techniques

• Assessing the caller's needs and triage for immediate safety or emergency medical attention of callers, or referrals to appropriate service referrals such as face-to-face crisis intervention, case management/advocacy services, individual therapy, or group services.

• Maintaining accurate and detailed call reports or, where applicable risk assessment reports, on key issues and referrals actioned.

• Where applicable or necessary, sign off on conducted risk assessments.

• Complying with responsibilities under the Data Protection Acts 1988, 2003 & 2018 (GDPR)

• Supporting in the development of appropriate crisis management plans to support callers in crisis.

• Make a quick in-the-moment decision on how to move forward if the responder is not sure how to proceed

• Ensuring smooth and diligent handover process to next shift personnel

• Dedicating entire shift to intellect tasks and responsibilities only

• Prepare psychological reports, risk summaries, and other clinical documentation as required

Requirements

Qualifications

• Master's Degree in Counselling/Counselling Psychology/Clinical Psychology or relevant mental health fields

• Active license with Australian Counselling Association (ACA), Psychotherapy and Counselling Federation of Australia (PACFA), or Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA)

• 1-3 years of experience on helplines (paid or volunteer), preferably in mental health or crisis settings

• Fluent communication skills in your native language; proficiency in additional languages is a plus

• Experience managing high-risk situations, including those at risk of suicide or in acute crisis

• Resilience and emotional composure under pressure, with the ability to recover from challenging interactionsations, ability to bounce back from stressful interactions and high-risk case

• Experience in clinical assessment, psychological report writing, and risk documentation

Preferred Qualifications

• Background in mental health or emergency services

• Completed training in Crisis Intervention or Suicide Prevention

• Proficiency in multiple languages

We’re a grassroots organization made up of people who support farms, food and families in Illinois.. Apply today to become a vital part of helping us advocate for Illinois agriculture and support Illinois farm families.
About the role
The intern will work alongside County Farm Bureau managers to help plan programs and events and learn what the role is all about.

- Help to plan events and programs for members
- Prepare information for board meetings
- Attend monthly board meetings
- Be in charge of completing a membership engagement project
- Work some nights and weekends

Application Timeline:
We know waiting can be difficult, so we want to set expectations upfront. Our internship recruiting process takes place over several months. Applications open in mid-September and are reviewed as they are received. HR interviews are expected to begin in mid-October, followed by interviews with hiring leaders. Depending on the role and applicant volume, hiring decisions and offers may be made anytime from October through January. We appreciate your patience throughout the process and will communicate updates as they become available.
How does this role make an impact?
"Test drive" a potential career path through real corporate projects, collaboration in meetings, and several networking opportunities. While working alongside and learning from expert leaders at all levels of the company, in addition to teaming up with fellow interns to showcase your ideas, our interns impact the business, and experience professional and personal growth.
Do you have what we're looking for?

• Pursuing a degree in agriculture or a related field.

• Must be able to work full-time hours from late May 2027 to early August 2027. The internship may be extended part-time through fall 2027 and spring 2028.

• Good Communicator

• Self-starter

• Organized

Why work with us?
Illinois Farm Bureau planted roots in 1916 and is one of the largest Farm Bureau organizations in the United States. Illinois Farm Bureau is a voice for Illinois farmers, farm families, and anyone involved in food and agriculture. That covers a lot of ground. Illinois Farm Bureau represents members in Springfield, IL and Washington D.C. When you become a part of Illinois Farm Bureau, you become part of something that touches the lives of people every day. You truly make a difference.
You’ll be able to take advantage of our benefits package, which includes insurance benefits (medical, dental, vision, disability, and life), 401(k) with company match, parental leave, paid time off, paid company holidays and time off to volunteer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, age, gender, sexual orientation, veteran status, national origin, disability, or any other status protected by applicable laws or regulations.

title: Manager, PLM and Product Data - PH
description:
THE ROLE
Gorilla Commerce is seeking a Manager, PLM & Product Data to serve as the business owner and super-user of the company's PLM platform.
Gorilla Commerce has successfully implemented PLM as the system of record for product specifications, BOMs, materials, suppliers and costing, and the platform is live across the sourcing organization. This role owns it from here - closing the residual data gaps that follow any implementation, raising the standard of governance, and maturing the platform through its next phases of capability.
The scope is broad but well supported. Sourcing teams own day-to-day data entry and maintenance following go-live. A dedicated analyst supports bulk uploads, reconciliation and heavy data work. IT leads the technical build of the PLM-ERP integration. This role sets the standards, makes the system decisions, and directs the work.
There is genuine white space here. An 18-month roadmap is defined - stronger specification and BOM structure, packaging and artwork governance, warning-label and claims data - and the person in this role will shape how it is prioritized, sequenced and delivered.
The role can be based globally and works core US Eastern hours to stay aligned with the VP and the wider team, with some flexibility for Asia-based sourcing partners.
This is not a data-entry or system-administration role. It is a product-data ownership role focused on structure, governance, adoption and system maturity.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
System Ownership & Configuration

• Own the day-to-day health, configuration and evolution of the PLM platform.

• Act as the internal authority on how PLM should be structured and used across parent and SKU hierarchy, specifications, BOMs, materials, supplier and factory records, quotes and costing.

• Determine whether an issue is best solved through configuration, data architecture, process design or vendor development.

• Own integration keys and mappings between PLM and the ERP.

Product Data Governance & Integrity

• Own product data quality as an ongoing discipline rather than a periodic cleanup.

• Establish validation standards, naming conventions and audit routines that prevent errors upstream.

• Reconcile PLM against ERP master data and resolve discrepancies at root cause.

• Close residual implementation gaps across product hierarchy, suppliers and factories, BOMs, color/size and supplier quote data.

Workflow, Change & Version Control

• Design and govern state models, approval workflows and revision control.

• Define how specification and BOM changes are requested, approved, tested and released.

• Assess downstream impact of data and configuration changes before release.

• Establish clear decision rights across this role, functional owners, IT and leadership.

Adoption, Training & Process Discipline

• Drive adoption across a distributed sourcing organization as a core deliverable of the role.

• Build and maintain SOPs, training materials and onboarding for new users.

• Move remaining product workflows off spreadsheets and email and into PLM.

• Identify recurring process failures and resolve the root cause rather than the symptom.

Vendor Partnership & Roadmap

• Own the day-to-day relationship with the PLM software vendor.

• Manage tickets, requirements, testing and feature scoping independently, escalating commercial matters to the VP.

• Own the business-side PLM roadmap and translate business needs into practical system and process solutions.

• Sequence future capability including deeper Level 2 and 3 BOM structure, packaging governance and claims data.

Integration Support

• Support the IT-led PLM-ERP integration through requirements definition, mapping validation and UAT.

• Diagnose whether issues originate in source data, PLM configuration, integration logic or the ERP.

• Keep integration keys complete and accurate across all active SKUs.

Our choices were built on a preference for strongly typed, functional languages and for serverless architectures -- choices that allow us to focus on the necessary, not the incidental, complexity of the problem space.
Some of the interesting engineering and design challenges in this problem space?

• How do you design a product that doesn't expose engineering concepts to users?

• How can you design an algorithm that can reliably locate elements on a page, without asking the user to specify css selectors?

title: Billing Manager

BILLING MANAGER

Our Mission For You

Own the invoicing engine of a hyper-growth energy-tech company. Your work directly protects our cash flow and keeps our growth engine running. Invoicing directly affects our cash flow in the millions. This role is a lever, not a cost center.

trawa enables mid-sized companies to access green, intelligent energy. We're a hyper-growth company with strong team growth, rising invoice volumes, and increasing complexity per invoice. Individual contracts, PPAs, spot, futures, EEG direct marketing, grid fees, taxes: every customer segment is a small puzzle. Today, that puzzle is solved mostly manually, and it needs to move to the next level.

You'll build order out of that complexity. You'll jump into individual invoices when it matters. At the same time, you'll design the process that makes those individual jumps unnecessary. You'll be part of our Billing Tool Rollout and help prepare invoicing for our ERP migration. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to own the operation, not just manage it.

What You'll Own

Own Invoicing End-to-End

- Own daily invoicing processes to trawa customers: quality, completeness, timing

- Reduce and eliminate our current ticket backlog through prioritization, root-cause analysis, and systematic execution

- Ensure complex billing logic (PPA, spot, futures, EEG direct marketing, grid fees, taxes) is correctly reflected in every invoice

- Own the invoicing KPIs: on-time rate, error rate, ticket aging, time-to-invoice

Build Scalable Processes

- Be part of designing and rolling out a scalable invoicing architecture, from today's manual setup to a standardized and automated solution

- Automate recurring process steps

- Document everything: reproducible, hand-off-ready, audit-ready

Stakeholder & Customer Communication

- Direct customer communication on invoicing questions, in writing (German and English)

- Partner closely with Sales and Customer Success to secure upstream data quality (contracts, prices, delivery points)

- Partner closely with our Tech/Data team, where consumption data, time series, and energy accruals are your input

- Establish escalation paths and priority logic with Sales and CS, so edge cases don't block the standard process

Data Quality & Handover to Accounting

- Ensure invoicing data flows cleanly into accounting, as the interface to our accounting team

- Contribute to month-end close: clean invoicing cut-off, documented open items, accruals-relevant data ready on time

- Audit-readiness from an invoicing perspective: process documentation, invoice-level traceability, controls

Your First 90 Days

Month 1, Land & Understand. Understand our business model, the German energy market basics, and our billing complexity. Understand what drives our corrections rate. Build relationships with the most important stakeholders.

Month 2, Stabilize. Keep invoicing running stably while spotting optimization opportunities. Define clear ticket priorities and escalation paths with Sales and CS. Ship first quick wins in automation and process design. Define and start tracking your KPIs: error rate, ticket aging.

Month 3, Build. Deliver a target process architecture for improvements to our current invoicing processes. Actively and proactively reduce time-to-invoice and corrections rates. Present your automation and process roadmap to the finance leadership team.

Who You Are

Must-haves

- 3+ years in Billing, Order-to-Cash, Finance Operations, or similar operational Finance roles

- Scale-up experience, with at least one station at a fast-growing company. You've worked without a clean ERP, with ambiguous processes, in a team being built as it runs

- B2B billing with complex pricing models, not SaaS flat-rate. You've handled individual contracts, volume-based logic, or formula-driven pricing

- Proven high-output track record. You've personally delivered and you can point to a moment where you built or saved a critical process

- Systems thin

title: People Operations Lead
description:

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we're changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK's leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We're growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we're hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We're on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll own the people engine room at Flock: the employee lifecycle, payroll input, benefits, the HRIS, the office and our in-person events. Your job is to design how a modern People function should work at a company where repetitive admin is automated out of existence and every process is simple, scalable and AI-native by default. You'll report to our Senior People Partner and work with everyone here, from a new joiner on day one to the CEO, who cares deeply about our culture.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

People Operations

- Own the full employee lifecycle: contracts, right-to-work, starter and leaver logistics, probations and changes. Shape the first day and first week alongside managers, delivering a strong employee experience across the lifecycle.

- Be the first point of contact for people queries and audits. Own the People inbox and core HR templates, and drive every query to resolution.

- Cut manual effort across the lifecycle by building AI-native workflows, so every routine people process is automated by default, then coach the business to use them. Own continuous improvement across People Ops.

- Partner with IT on joiner and leaver access automation, and on cost and data audits.

Office Management & Socials

- Run the office environment and vendor relationships, including routine upkeep like weekly snack orders and post. Cover health and safety as a trained First Aider and Fire Marshal, and provision hardware fast.

- Own the company social calendar and rituals, from bi-weekly Flock o'Clock (working closely with the CEO) to quarterly Town Halls and larger events, keeping them engaging and on budget.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

- Hands-on People or HR Operations experience, ideally in a fast-moving scale-up, with real ownership of end-to-end processes. CIPD or equivalent experience required.

- Hands-on payroll input and benefits administration. HiBob experience is a plus.

- Strong HRIS skills across workflows, automations and integrations, plus confident data and spreadsheet ability.

- Real evidence of building with AI: workflows or tools you've shipped and use, not ones you've only read about.

- Low ego and high standards. You care most that the work is right and well run.

YOUR ROLE

We’re hiring a Sales Development Representative to own the front half of our sales funnel-but this isn’t a pure dial-for-dollars role. You’ll generate and qualify pipeline from fund managers across venture capital and private equity, while partnering hands-on with our Account Executives as deals move through the middle of the funnel.

You’ll help prepare specialised decks, tailor materials, and keep opportunities moving. This is a role for someone who wants full visibility into how a B2B sales cycle works, not just the first five minutes of it.

TOP OF FUNNEL

- Research and prioritise target accounts by assets under management, fund stage, vehicle type, and geography

- Own and maintain signal sources such as new-fund announcements and regulator registers, including BaFin, the FCA, and the CSSF

- Run outbound campaigns across email, LinkedIn, and calls to generate qualified conversations for accounts not already activated by Account Executives

- Qualify inbound leads against our ideal customer profile and book meetings for Account Executives

- Keep HubSpot pristine, with accurate stages, notes, and next steps for every touchpoint

- Deliver against weekly and monthly activity and pipeline-generation targets

MID FUNNEL

- Partner with Account Executives to prepare for deep dives and workshops by pulling together GP and fund research, competitive context, and meeting briefs

- Build and tailor pitch decks, one-pagers, and proposal materials for specific prospects

- 1-3 years of experience in an SDR, BDR, or sales-support role, ideally in private markets, fintech, or financial services

- Sales Navigator, HubSpot, and AI tools such as Claude, Granola, or equivalent are part of your daily workbench-not occasional aids

- You can build repeatable systems to monitor signals across regulator registers and hundreds of accounts rather than working through them manually

- Comfortable writing sharp outbound copy and building clean, persuasive decks in Google Slides

- Strong organisational instincts-you keep details, documents, and next steps from falling through the cracks

- Genuine curiosity about private markets and fund structures; prior exposure to venture capital, private equity, or fund administration is a strong plus, not a requirement

- CRM fluency, with HubSpot preferred

- Excellent written and verbal English

NICE TO HAVE

- Experience selling to fund managers, general partners, or asset managers

- Familiarity with fund administration, compliance, or fund-operations concepts

WORKPLACE & BENEFITS

- Customisable benefits package covering wellbeing, sport, mobility, food, and more

- 28 days of vacation, plus 2 company days and local public holidays

- Up to 6 remote calendar weeks a year

- A great tech and work setup

- Work with a diverse team of 130+ bunchies from 40+ countries, with leaders who are best-in-class in their domains

HIRING PROCESS

1. People Team Interview (30 min) - Meet us, share what you’re looking for, and explore whether the role and bunch feel like the right mutual fit.

2. Commercial Deep Dive (30 min) - Discuss your sales experience, how you create and qualify pipeline, and how you partner with AEs to move opportunities forward.

3. Case Study with our Head of Sales (45 min) - Work through a practical, role-relevant scenario and show how you research accounts, prioritise opportunities, communicate clearly, and turn information into action.

We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

title: Social Worker – Mental Health
description:
Our client based in Neath Port Talbot is seeking an experienced Social Worker to join their Mental Health Team. This is an excellent opportunity for a skilled practitioner to work with adults experiencing mental health needs, supporting them to achieve positive outcomes, maximise independence, and improve their wellbeing through strengths-based and person-centred practice.

The successful candidate will work closely with individuals, carers, families, health professionals, and partner agencies to assess needs, coordinate services, manage risk, and develop effective support plans. Working within a multidisciplinary environment, you will play a key role in safeguarding vulnerable adults, promoting recovery, facilitating access to community resources, and ensuring individuals remain at the centre of all decision-making.

This role requires a confident Social Worker with strong assessment skills, experience of complex case management, and a comprehensive understanding of mental health practice, safeguarding, capacity assessments, and partnership working.

What will your responsibilities be?

In this role, you will:

• Managing a complex caseload of adults with mental health needs, ensuring timely and effective social work interventions.

• Undertaking strengths-based assessments in partnership with individuals, families, carers, and professionals to identify needs, risks, and desired outcomes.

• Developing, implementing, coordinating, and reviewing person-centred care and support plans that promote recovery, independence, and wellbeing.

• Identifying and utilising community resources, natural support networks, and local services to support individuals in achieving their outcomes.

• Working collaboratively with health professionals, partner agencies, carers, and community organisations to deliver coordinated care and support.

• Undertaking Mental Capacity Assessments and facilitating Best Interest decision-making in accordance with the Mental Capacity Act.

• Completing Continuing Healthcare (CHC) assessments and contributing to multidisciplinary eligibility processes where required.

• Undertaking safeguarding enquiries and initiating appropriate action to protect adults at risk from abuse, neglect, exploitation, and self-neglect.

• Carrying out risk assessments and applying Positive Risk Taking principles to support individuals safely and effectively.

• Conducting non-criminal investigations as part of Adult at Risk processes and safeguarding procedures.

• Attending and contributing to case conferences, multidisciplinary meetings, reviews, and safeguarding meetings, providing a professional social work perspective.

• Chairing reviews, meetings, and case conferences where required.

• Undertaking financial assessments in accordance with relevant charging frameworks and policies.

• Supporting hospital discharge planning and community-based interventions to prevent unnecessary admissions where appropriate.

• Maintaining accurate, timely, and legally compliant case recording, assessments, reports, and documentation.

• Contributing to service development, team learning, continuous improvement initiatives, and professional development activities.

• Supporting colleagues with complex casework and providing guidance on high-risk situations and interventions where required.

• Undertaking Approved Mental Health Professional duties if qualified and required by the service.

Qualifications & Experience:

• Professional Qualification: Degree in Social Work, Diploma in Social Work, CQSW, CSS, or equivalent recognised Social Work qualification.

• Registration: Must be registered with Social Care Wales.

• Experience: Significant post-qualified experience within Adult Mental Health Services or Adult Social Care.

• Mental Health Experience: Proven experience working with adults experiencing complex and enduring mental health needs.

title: Vertriebsmitarbeiter (m/w/d) in der Telefonakquise
description:
Hörer in die Hand, wählen, pitchen, Termin. Nochmal. Und nochmal. Und am Ende des Tages weißt du genau, was du geleistet hast - weil deine Ergebnisse messbar sind. Wenn sich das für dich nicht nach Arbeit, sondern nach Antrieb anhört, dann lies weiter.
Wir suchen keinen, der Kaltakquise „auch mal machen kann". Wir suchen jemanden, der sie liebt. Der den Kick spürt, wenn ein Entscheider nach 30 Sekunden zuhört statt aufzulegen. Der Einwände nicht als Problem sieht, sondern als Spielfeld.
Bei Clementine Media helfen wir Kommunen in ganz Deutschland, ihre offenen Stellen zu besetzen - mithilfe von Neuro-Recruiting, das wirklich funktioniert.
Über 150 Städte und Gemeinden vertrauen uns bereits. Dein Job: Bürgermeister, Hauptamtsleiter und Personalchefs ans Telefon bekommen und qualifizierte Termine für unser Vertriebsteam setzen.
Du öffnest die Tür - wir machen den Rest.
Aufgaben

• Du kontaktierst proaktiv Städte, Gemeinden und Landkreise per Telefon und identifizierst den richtigen Ansprechpartner (Bürgermeister, Geschäftsführer, Hauptamtsleiter, Personalverantwortliche).

• Du führst professionelle Erstgespräche am Telefon, weckst Interesse an unserer Recruiting-Lösung und positionierst Clementine Media als kompetenten Partner.

• Du vereinbarst qualifizierte Termine - das ist dein zentrales Ziel und deine wichtigste Kennzahl.

• Du pflegst deine Kontakte und Gesprächsergebnisse sauber in unserem CRM-System (Close CRM) und hältst deine Pipeline aktuell.

• Du arbeitest mit einem erprobten Gesprächsleitfaden, den du mit der Zeit zu deinem eigenen machst und kontinuierlich verbesserst.

• Du wirkst aktiv bei der Optimierung unser Vertriebsprozesse mit.

Qualifikation

• Du hast Erfahrung in der telefonischen Kaltakquise, im Telefonvertrieb oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle (z. B. SDR, BDR, Call Agent, Terminierung) - idealerweise im B2B-Umfeld.

• Du sprichst fließend Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau - am Telefon klingst du professionell, sympathisch und überzeugend.

• Du hast keine Scheu vor dem Hörer und lässt dich von einem „Nein" nicht aus der Ruhe bringen. Hartnäckigkeit mit Fingerspitzengefühl ist deine Stärke.

• Du arbeitest strukturiert, organisierst dich selbstständig und behältst auch bei hohem Anrufvolumen den Überblick.

• Du bist sicher im Umgang mit CRM-Systemen und digitalen Tools.

• Erfahrung im öffentlichen Sektor oder Kommunalvertrieb ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss - wir bringen dir alles Nötige bei.

Benefits

•
100 % Remote - arbeite von dort, wo du am produktivsten bist (innerhalb Deutschlands).

•
Erprobtes System - du bekommst einen bewährten Gesprächsleitfaden, Schulungen und ein CRM, das für dich arbeitet.

•
Sinnvolle Arbeit - du hilfst Kommunen, die Menschen zu finden, die den öffentlichen Dienst am Laufen halten: Erzieher, Ingenieure, Verwaltungskräfte.

•
Wachsendes Unternehmen - über 130 Kommunen vertrauen uns bereits. Sei Teil unseres nächsten Wachstumsschritts.

•
Attraktive Vergütung ohne Deckel - solides Fixgehalt plus unbegrenzte Provisionen. Je mehr qualifizierte Termine du setzt, desto mehr verdienst du - ohne Obergrenze.

•
Kurze Wege, flache Hierarchien - du arbeitest direkt mit der Geschäftsführung zusammen und hast echten Einfluss.

Du brauchst kein langes Anschreiben. Bewirb dich einfach - wir melden uns schnell. Wenn du der Typ bist, der lieber anruft als E-Mails zu schreiben, dann zeig uns genau das. Wir freuen uns, von dir zu hören.

title: Preparador/a de oposiciones del Área Social (Trabajo Social, Educación Social, P
description:
🚀 Únete al claustro de preparadores de Polaris x Ucademy

¿Eres trabajador/a social, educador/a social u otro profesional del ámbito social con plaza, o preparas estas oposiciones? Colabora en remoto con Polaris x Ucademy .
🤝 Buscamos preparadores/as para las oposiciones del Área Social
Queremos construir un claustro de preparadores especializados en el Área Social , en el que cada profesional aporte su experiencia en su categoría y en las administraciones que mejor conoce.
No necesitas dominar todas las oposiciones ni todas las administraciones. Buscamos a quien conozca a fondo una o varias.
📚 Oposiciones para las que buscamos preparadores
⭐ Categorías principales

• Trabajo Social (A2)

• Educación Social (A2)

También buscamos preparadores de

• Psicología (A1)

• Terapia Ocupacional (A2)

• Integración Social (C1 / Técnico Superior)

• Animación Sociocultural (C1 / Técnico Superior)

🏛️ Una misma profesión, muchas convocatorias
Estas oposiciones las convocan administraciones muy distintas, y cada una tiene su temario, su legislación y su forma de examinar. Trabajo Social, por ejemplo, puede salir en el Estado, en una comunidad autónoma, en un ayuntamiento, en Instituciones Penitenciarias, en la Seguridad Social o en un servicio de salud.
Por eso buscamos especialmente preparadores que conozcan procesos selectivos de:

• Administración General del Estado

• Comunidades Autónomas

• Administración Local / Ayuntamientos

• Instituciones Penitenciarias

• Seguridad Social

• Sanidad

• Otros organismos públicos

En las convocatorias autonómicas y locales, la legislación de cada comunidad marca la diferencia. Por eso queremos contar con preparadores de todas las comunidades autónomas , que conozcan de primera mano la normativa y los procesos de su territorio.
🌟 Quiénes somos
En Polaris x Ucademy preparamos oposiciones de una forma más digital, práctica y personalizada. Ya hemos acompañado a miles de opositores y tenemos un objetivo claro: que 10.000 personas consigan su plaza preparándose con nosotros .
Para lograrlo, estamos ampliando nuestro claustro de preparadores de alto rendimiento .
Somos muy digitales, pero lo humano no se negocia . La tecnología nos ayuda a enseñar mejor, y son nuestros preparadores quienes aportan conocimiento, criterio, cercanía y acompañamiento.
🔎 A quién buscamos

• Profesionales del ámbito social con plaza (funcionarios/as o personal laboral fijo, en activo o en excedencia) en alguna de estas categorías.

• Preparadores/as con experiencia en estas oposiciones.

•
Personas capaces de trabajar las dos caras de la oposición :

• el contenido propio de la profesión (intervención, metodología, recursos, ética…),

• y la legislación y el contenido específico de la administración que convoca, incluida la normativa autonómica de su comunidad.

• Quienes dominen los supuestos prácticos , clave en la mayoría de estas oposiciones.

• Quienes sepan enseñar y acompañar : explicar con claridad, dar feedback útil y ayudar a sostener la preparación.

• Soltura con herramientas digitales . Si ya utilizas IA en tu día a día, mucho mejor.

🎯 En qué podrás colaborar
Según tu categoría, las administraciones que conozcas y tu disponibilidad, podrás participar en uno o varios proyectos:

• Clases online del temario profesional y del temario específico de cada administración.

• Supuestos prácticos: diseñarlos, resolverlos y corregir los de los alumnos.

• Legislación específica (servicios sociales, dependencia, menores, igualdad, ejecución penal, Seguridad Social…) según la convocatoria.

• Preguntas tipo test y simulacros con el formato real.

• Preparación de pruebas orales o de defensa , cuando la convocatoria las incluya.

• Seguimiento de alumnos: resolver dudas y ayudarles a avanzar.

• Temarios, esquemas, resúmenes y vídeos cortos.

🤝 Cómo funciona la colaboración
No es un puesto de trabajo a jornada completa ni parcial. Colaborarás con Polaris x Ucademy mediante prestación de servicios en proyectos educa

description:
Why This Role Matters
As Principal, Business Operations at Greenbox Capital , you will help define how the company operates, scales, and makes decisions.
You will transform ambiguous business problems into clear workflows, operating models, business rules, implementation requirements, and measurable operating outcomes across underwriting, renewals, funding, servicing, sales, risk, product, data, and technology.
This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who can move from diagnosis through implementation. You will identify operational friction, design future-state processes, align cross-functional stakeholders, support rollout and adoption, and measure whether the change deliveredmeaningful business impact.
AI and automation may be used where appropriate, but they are not the identity of the role. The core focus is business-process transformation, adoption, and measurable improvement.
What Success Looks Like

• Transform complex or inconsistent workflows into scalable, adopted operating processes.

• Reduce friction, rework, delays, manual touches, and unclear ownership.

• Improve outcomes tied to conversion, productivity, speed, capacity, customer or broker experience, risk controls, margin, or cost efficiency.

• Lead workflow redesign from initial diagnosis through pilot, rollout, adoption, and measurement.

• Build alignment across executives, frontline teams, and Product, Technology, Data, Engineering, and Operations.

• Connect process changes to a clear business case, measurable outcomes, and sustained usage.

• Create business rules, controls, handoffs, and implementation requirements that teams and systems can execute consistently.
What You’ll Do:
Diagnose and Prioritize Opportunities

• Investigate operational friction across underwriting, renewals, funding, servicing, sales, risk, product, data, and customer or broker workflows.

• Interview stakeholders to understand current processes, decision logic, handoffs, controls, pain points, and exceptions.

• Identify the root causes behind delays, leakage, rework, inconsistent execution, data gaps, unclear ownership, and adoption challenges.

• Prioritize opportunities based on business impact, ROI, customer or broker experience, risk, scalability, and implementation feasibility.
Design Future-State Workflows

• Redesign workflows, handoffs, decision paths, escalation rules, controls, exception processes, and operating rhythms.

• Define roles, responsibilities, decision rights, operating definitions, and governance expectations.

• Align stakeholders on the future-state process before technology or automation is applied.

• Determine where a process needs better design, clearer rules, stronger data, human judgment, simple automation, or AI-enabled support.
Define Business Rules and Implementation Requirements

• Capture business rules, decision paths, workflows, handoffs, operating definitions, controls, and implementation requirements.

• Use clear, structured formats such as process maps, decision trees, SOPs, tables, responsibility matrices, or rules documentation.

• Translate business needs into actionable requirements for Product, Technology, Data, Engineering, AI Operations, and operational teams.

• Define KPIs, leading indicators, adoption measures, ROI logic, and reporting requirements.

• Improve clarity and traceability across system fields, workflow statuses, routing logic, manual overrides, exception paths, and controls.
Lead Implementation and Adoption

• Drive cross-functional execution from diagnosis through design, pilot, rollout, adoption, and measurement.

• Create implementation plans, stakeholder communications, SOP updates, training materials, and enablement resources.

• Influence teams and drive behavior change without direct authority.

• Identify risks, manage tradeoffs, escalate blockers, and maintain accountability across stakeholders.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Session Replay | USA | Remote
description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X .

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote position. We are looking for candidates in the USA time zones.

Senior Software Engineer - Session Replay

The Opportunity:

The Session Replay squad is building a new Grafana Cloud product that helps our customers to understand what users actually experienced when something goes wrong.

Session Replay connects frontend signals (errors, performance, synthetic checks) to concrete session-level evidence, enabling faster and more confident investigation of production issues.

This team works at the intersection of:

• frontend observability,

• backend data processing and storage at scale,

• debugging workflows across products,

• privacy and access control,

• performance and cost constraints at scale.

Session Replay is still early, which means you’ll help shape both what we build and how it fits into Grafana Cloud. A key part of our next phase is evolving the backend architecture of capturing sessions, including a migration toward columnar/analytical solution as a primary storage and query engine for high-volume session data.

As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a new perspective to the software. We are looking for Senior Software Engineers who are passionate about working with data and providing seamless experiences for our customers to join our growing team! Our stack is Golang, Typescript and React, but we build tools for people using many other stacks. 

What You’ll Be Doing:

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will operate as a technical leader and systems thinker, driving both product direction and architectural evolution, specifically, you will:

• Own end-to-end technical direction for Session Replay, spanning frontend, backend, and data systems

• Drive the evolution of our backend architecture, including:

• Designing systems around columnar/analytical data storage for large-scale session data  

• Defining data models, ingestion pipelines, and query patterns

• Lead the design of investigation workflows, connecting replay with logs, metrics, traces and other telemetry across Grafana Cloud

• Make high-leverage architectural decisions that impact multiple teams and products

• Partner with teams across Grafana (Frontend Observability, Synthetic Monitoring, Core Grafana) to build cohesive cross-product experiences

• Engage directly with customers - joining calls, gathering structured feedback, and helping customers instrument and adopt Session Replay successfully. 

• Improve engineering standards, patterns, and operational practices

title: Marketing Manager
description:

We ignite the passions of global sports fans and maximize the presence and reach for our hundreds of sports partners globally by offering products and services across Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, and Fanatics Betting & Gaming, allowing sports fans to Buy, Collect, and Bet. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally. 

 

About the Team

Fanatics Collectibles is a new company operating at the intersection of collectibles, culture, and technology. Backed by world-class investors, operators, and sports & entertainment partners, we are building the global leader in next-generation collectibles. Together, we are reimagining every part of the collectibles experience for fans, partners, and creators.

Role Summary

Fanatics Collectibles is seeking a Marketing Manager who will be responsible for leading the company’s marketing strategy, primarily focused on the Brazilian market, with additional reach into other Latin American countries. • Develop and execute the company’s marketing plan, focusing on brand growth, consumer engagement, and sales.

• Manage relationships with agencies, vendors, and strategic partners.

• Collaborate closely with the product, sales, design, and licensing teams to ensure cohesive go-to-market efforts.

• Monitor KPIs and prepare analytical reports to support data-driven decision-making.

• Develop initiatives to strengthen the relationship with the collector community.

• Ensure consistent brand representation across all channels and touchpoints.

Requirements:

• Bachelor’s degree in marketing, Communications, Advertising, Business Administration, or related fields.

• Minimum of 5 years of experience in marketing, including leadership roles.

• Background in sports, entertainment, collectibles, or licensing industries is preferred.

• Dynamic, creative, results-oriented, and highly hands-on profile.

• Strong knowledge of digital marketing, branding, e-commerce, media campaigns, and CRM.

• Willingness to travel occasionally.

Nice to Have:

• Passion for sports, pop culture, and collectibles.

The Legal, Risk & Compliance (LRC) team at Airwallex is a collaborative group of legal minds and risk management experts. We're passionate about safeguarding Airwallex's operations, fostering a culture of compliance and ethical conduct, and ensuring we navigate the global financial landscape with integrity. title: US Congressional Lead

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We believe that achieving our goal requires effective engagement with public policy stakeholders and the broader community impacted by AI. Accordingly, our Global Affairs team builds authentic, collaborative relationships with public officials and the broader AI policymaking community to inform and support our shared work in these domains. We ensure that insights from policymakers inform our work and - in collaboration with our colleagues and external stakeholders - seek to further regulation, industry standards, and safe and beneficial development of AI tools.

About the Role

As a US Congressional Lead on the Global Affairs team, you will help develop strategies and advance OpenAI’s engagement with the U.S. Congress across a range of legislative and policy priorities. You will develop and manage relationships with House and Senate lawmakers and staff, with particular attention to committees shaping technology and emerging policy issues. You will support OpenAI’s U.S. Global Affairs team in meetings, briefings, hearings, and other engagements, and collaborate with civil society and industry partners in alignment with OpenAI’s mission.

OpenAI releases industry-leading research and tools. You will face new challenges as the impact of cutting edge generative AI technologies continues to be explored and as the needs of the organization evolve. Day-to-day work may encompass tracking emerging congressional policy issues, coordinating complex cross-functional engagement with legal, policy, and communications teams, developing briefing materials, preparing our leaders for congressional hearings and other government engagements, and representing OpenAI in private and public forums.

We are looking for a self-directed and creative individual with substantial Capitol Hill experience, strong congressional relationships, experience managing private sector and civil society relationships, and an understanding of AI-related legislative and regulatory issues and processes.

This role is based in Washington, DC and may require frequent travel to participate in meetings and events with key stakeholders.

- Are well versed in the issues around emerging AI technologies, particularly as they relate to congressional policymaking.

- Are an enthusiastic and effective coalition builder who thrives as a member of a high performing, peer-led global team.

- Are highly organized, and are used to working as an accountable individual contributor as well as a team player.

- Are passionate about the promise of technology and the future of artificial intelligence but thoughtful about its potential risks.

We're looking for a blend of:

- Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of the U.S. government, its institutions and legislative processes, and the key policy issues and debates related to AI.

- Sound judgment and outstanding personal integrity

title: Threat Investigator
description:
About 10a Labs : 10a Labs is the safety and threat-intelligence layer trusted by frontier AI labs, AI unicorns, Fortune 10 companies, and leading global technology platforms. Our adversarial red teaming, model evaluations, and intelligence collection enable engineering, safety, and security teams to stay ahead of evolving threats and deploy AI systems safely.

10a Labs ’ Investigations Team is seeking additional support to respond to critical safety incidents and conduct investigations across a range of abuse areas, including but not limited to violence, hate, mental health, CBRNE, child safety, and cyber abuse.
This role requires the ability to work Pacific Time (PT) hours and have valid work authorization in the United States.
About the Role:
As a Threat Investigator , you will be supporting our Investigations Team and responsible for detecting and/or responding to malicious uses and abuse, investigating the activity, drafting reports based on your findings, and making recommendations. This will require technical experience investigating threat actors, harmful behaviors, and/or other activities; as well as a strong ability to use SQL and Python to query, transform, and understand data. You will also respond to escalations and reactive leads, including those that are not caught by our existing safety systems.
Investigations involve sensitive and distressing content, including sexual, violent, or otherwise-disturbing material.
This role includes serving in an on-call capacity that will involve resolving urgent escalations outside of normal work hours, occasionally including evenings and weekends. The typical on-call rotation is 7 consecutive days per 2 months, though this may shift based on operational needs and candidates should be prepared to remain flexible.
This is a remote, full-time position.
In this role, you will:

• Proactively detect and reacquire bad actors on our platform.

• Investigate potentially policy-violating activity by querying internal data sources (using SQL and Python) and cross-referencing open source information (OSINT).

• Document and share investigative findings with internal stakeholders.

Requirements:

• At least 3+ years of related investigative experience in Trust & Safety, National Security, Defense, Intelligence, or Law Enforcement domains working on related topics; must be willing to work on sensitive subject matter including child safety.

• U.S.-based, with the ability to work West Coast hours (9am - 5pm PT).

• Ability to be on-call that will involve resolving urgent escalations outside of normal work hours, including occasional evenings and weekends.

• Strong SQL and Python proficiency and/or additional programming skills.

• Strong and applicable technical investigative skillset with ability to develop and maintain detection pipelines.

• Ability to rapidly context switch across domains, modalities, and abuse areas.

• Excited to work in a fast paced, ambiguous, and purposeful space with high impact across users and beyond.

Preferred Qualities (but not required):

• Expertise with risk and abuse related to AI platforms.

• Full professional proficiency in Arabic, Chinese, Farsi, Portuguese, Russian, or Spanish.

• Have experience scaling and automating detection and mitigation processes.

• Familiarity using language models to scale.

• Familiarity with one of the following topics/areas: violence, extremism,, child safety, digital mental health, scams and fraud abuse, radicalization/persuasion/grooming, hateful activities and groups.

title: System Administrator – SME (Cloud, Hybrid)
description:
Responsibilities
Peraton is seeking an experienced System Administrator - Subject Matter Expert (SME) specializing in cloud and hybrid computing environments to support the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) at the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). In this senior-level role, you will serve as a key technical advisor and hands-on administrator across a complex hybrid infrastructure spanning on-premises data center environments and multi-cloud platforms including Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform.
Work location: Remote
What You Will Do:

• Hybrid Systems Administration: Administer and maintain Windows Server and Linux/UNIX-based operating systems (Red Hat, Ubuntu, macOS, and comparable distributions) running on enterprise hardware including Dell, HP x86, and Oracle SPARC platforms across multiple physical data centers.

• Virtualization Management: Administer VMware vCloud, vSphere, vCenter, and Enterprise Plus virtualization environments; manage VMware Operations (vROPS) and Log Insight for performance monitoring, optimization, and troubleshooting; support System Center Virtual Machine Manager (SCVMM) as needed.

• Cloud Administration & Optimization: Administer and optimize AWS environments (EC2, S3, CloudFormation, Application Migration Service, and related services); provide expert guidance on cloud and cluster computing architectures; research, evaluate, and deploy advanced cloud computing capabilities and large-data analytics solutions for the program.

• Migration & Modernization: Lead and support data integration and workload migration efforts from on-premises infrastructure to cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP); document migration paths, develop runbooks, and execute cutovers with minimal-to-no customer downtime.

• Storage & Backup/DR Administration: Administer NAS and SAN storage devices; manage enterprise backup software; implement and maintain Backup-to-Cloud replication and disaster recovery (DR) solutions to meet program continuity requirements.

• Architecture Advisory: Advise OCIO leadership and program stakeholders on cloud and hybrid computing architectures, system and memory management optimization across distributed platforms, and best practices for workload placement and resource utilization.

• Security & Patch Management: Apply OS, hypervisor, and application-level security patches to resolve vulnerabilities; maintain compliance with DOI/USGS security standards and Information Assurance Vulnerability Alert (IAVA) remediation timelines.

• Monitoring, Observability & Incident Response: Design and maintain operational monitoring dashboards (vROPS, Datadog, CloudWatch, or comparable tools) for CPU, memory, and storage utilization; troubleshoot and resolve performance and availability incidents across physical, virtual, and cloud infrastructure.

• DevOps & Automation Support: Leverage container and automation tooling (Kubernetes, Jenkins, Ansible, or comparable platforms) to support workload modernization, CI/CD pipeline operations, and infrastructure-as-code deployments.

• Documentation & Collaboration: Maintain accurate technical documentation including architecture diagrams, configuration records, migration plans, and runbooks; collaborate using Government-provided tools (Jira, Confluence, Microsoft Teams).

Qualifications
Basic Qualifications:

• Bachelors degree and 10 years professional experience, or a Masters degree and 8 years professional experience, or an Associates degree and 12 years professional experience; or a high school diploma/equivalent and 14 years’ professional experience.

• U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance; all work must be performed within the United States

• Extensive experience in systems administration across hybrid IT environments (on-premises + cloud).

• VMware Virtualization: Demonstrated expertise administering vCenter, ESXi/vSphere (6.x/7.x/8.x), vROPS, and VMware

title: Prototype Manufacturing Engineer, Mechanical & Fluid Systems
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S) Manufacturing Engineering team is seeking a Prototype Manufacturing Engineer to execute first builds and prototype manufacturing across our mechanical, structural, thermal management, and fluid systems (fuel, hydraulics, pneumatics) subsystems. This role spans the full AD&S portfolio of autonomous aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering munitions - and is designed for an engineer who thrives in ambiguity, builds hardware with incomplete inputs, and treats every first build as an opportunity to generate the manufacturing knowledge that makes future production possible.

As a Prototype ME, you are the first manufacturing engineer on a new build. You will work from incomplete design definitions - often without released drawings or established work instructions - to figure out how hardware goes together, build the first units, and document what you learn. Your output is not just a built prototype; it is the MVP work instructions, preliminary BOM structure, buildability feedback, and lessons learned that the DFx and SME teams use to drive producibility improvements and prepare for rate production. You are the bridge between a design engineer's intent and the physical reality of how something gets built for the first time.

This is a cross-program role. You will move between AD&S programs based on where first builds are happening, bringing a consistent methodology to new hardware regardless of the product line. You will work closely with design engineers, DFx engineers, SME manufacturing engineers, and production technicians. The pace is fast, the inputs are messy, and the expectation is that you bring order to chaos - one build at a time.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Execute first builds of new mechanical, structural, thermal, and fluid system hardware across AD&S programs, working from preliminary or incomplete design inputs (unreleased models, draft drawings, verbal direction from design engineers).

• Develop MVP work instructions during and immediately after first builds - capturing assembly sequences, tooling needs, critical dimensions, torque values, and process notes sufficient for a technician to repeat the build.

• Establish preliminary BOM structures (Make/Buy determinations) based on first-build experience, identifying which components should be fabricated internally, procured, or sent to contract manufacturers.

• Provide structured design feedback to design engineers based on first-build observations - specifically addressing buildability, checkability (can you inspect it?), and repeatability (can someone else build it the same way?).

• Document lessons learned from every first build and feed them directly to DFx engineers for incorporation into formal DFM/DFA reviews and design trade studies.

• Build and support Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) units - Ironbirds, Copperbirds, and similar integration test articles - where the build method is undefined and must be figured out from scratch.

• Identify and resolve manufacturing issues in real time on the shop floor during first builds, including fit/interference problems, fastener access issues, routing conflicts, and assembly sequence challenges.

- Define and communicate the product strategy and roadmap for Licensing & Billing in partnership with Engineering, Product leadership, Finance, and go-to-market.

- Prioritize foundational investments based on revenue integrity, enterprise needs, data correctness, and engineering effort, and make trade-offs explicit.

- Lead discovery with enterprise customers, Sales, Customer Success, Finance, and RevOps to understand how n8n is bought, renewed, and grown today, and where that breaks.

LICENSING, ENTITLEMENTS & ACCOUNTS

- Own the license server and entitlement model: issuance, renewal, and validation across Cloud, self-hosted, air-gapped, and OEM deployments, with one source of truth for which plan or deal grants which features.

- Introduce "account" as a first-class product primitive (accounts, purchases, license keys, activations) and expose it as the API contract our customer-facing console and multi-instance management are built on.

- Productize the deal-to-entitlement flow so a closed deal in Salesforce creates or updates entitlements without manual steps.

METERING & BILLING PLATFORM

- Own usage metering and billing for Cloud and Enterprise, including subscription billing: what counts as a billable execution, quota consumption, and overage charging.

- Lead the migration off Paddle Classic and unify Cloud and Enterprise billing into one platform.

- Build the mechanics for usage-based enterprise billing and reliable overage charging.

CROSS-ORG ALIGNMENT

- Make the architecture and mechanism decisions (entitlement model, billing platform, enterprise invoicing path) and align closely with Finance and go-to-market on each of them. Every decision here touches money; you bring people along rather than inform them afterwards.

- Hold clear boundaries with adjacent teams: the customer console, execution limits, and access control live elsewhere; you own the data and mechanics they rely on.

- Establish clear success measures and keep the squad accountable for outcomes, not only delivery.

title: Deployed Engineer (Boston)
description:
ABOUT US

At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.

With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.

Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Deployed Engineering team works directly with companies building and running AI agents in production, helping turn ideas and prototypes into systems teams can rely on.

This is a hands-on, highly technical team that partners closely with customer engineers across the full lifecycle, from pre-sales evaluations to post-deployment advisory work. The focus is on achieving the technical win, co-designing agent architectures, and helping customers operate agents reliably at scale using the LangChain suite.

Deployed Engineers sit at the intersection of engineering, product, and go-to-market, shaping how LangChain is adopted in the field and feeding real-world insights back into the platform.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Deployed Engineer…You’ll work on some of the hardest problems in applied AI - not demos, not research, but systems that real teams depend on in production. The feedback loop is fast, the impact is visible, and the work you do directly shapes how AI agents are built in the real world.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Co-architect and co-build production AI agents with customer engineering teams

- Own the technical win in pre-sales by designing POCs, answering deep technical questions, and guiding evaluations

- Help customers deploy and operate agent-based applications such as conversational agents, research agents, and multi-step workflows

- Advise customers post-sale on architecture, best practices, and roadmap-level decisions

- Run technical demos, trainings, and workshops for developer audiences

- Surface field feedback and contribute reusable patterns, cookbooks, and example code that scale across customers

- Occasionally contribute code upstream when it meaningfully improves customer outcomes

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

- 3+ years in a relevant technical role (software engineering, customer engineering, solutions engineering, founding/product engineering), ideally in a startup or scale-up

- Strong Python, JavaScript and systems fundamentals

- Have designed agent-based or LLM-powered applications beyond simple API calls, including multi-step workflows, orchestration, and failure handling

- Are comfortable working directly with customers during POCs, architecture reviews, and technical evaluations

- Can explain technical tradeoffs clearly and build trust with developer audiences

- Take responsibility for outcomes, not just recommendations

- Have a bias toward action and enjoy figuring things out as you go

- Are excited about operating AI agents in production, not just building demos

NICE TO HAVE’S:

- You’ve deployed AI agents in production, especially using LangChain, LangGraph, or similar frameworks

- Worked with

title: Principal Analyst, Enterprise Architecture
description:
At Forrester, we’re trusted to work on trailblazing, mission critical problems that business and technology leaders face today. That’s why we’re always looking to empower talented individuals to perform at their best every single day. We’re proud of our community of smart people and vibrant voices who come together to do what’s right by our clients and each other. Our success is driven by curiosity, courage and customer obsession. The confidence and drive to be bold at work. Join us and build an extraordinary future.
About This Role:
Forrester Research is seeking a Principal Analyst to be a critical member of the research team responsible for leading our Enterprise Solutions Architecture Practice, part of our Technology Architecture & Delivery Research Group. This practice serves CIOs, CTOs and IT Leaders and Practitioners helping them achieve high performance - the ability to deliver great business results through technology. The Principal Analyst delivers research that encompasses: 1) Enterprise Architecture practice, strategy and portfolio of research
2) Drive research on key platforms, vendors and trends
3) Brings the right mix of both strategic and technical architecture and delivery experiences
4) fosters a culture of collaboration across our Research, Sales, Product and Customer Success teams.

The Principal Analyst has a strong understanding of CIO/CTO concerns and priorities, helps them understand the implications of technology, economies, labor, and other key trends on IT strategy and delivery.
Job Description:
The Principal Analyst works as part of a high-performing team with a strong emphasis on collaborating with others in all aspects of the job. A Principal Analyst is expected to:

• Lead the Enterprise Solutions Architecture practice area, working across Forrester research teams, including the Technology Strategy and Executive Partner teams as well as Sales and Product to develop a complete research portfolio that drives customer delight and revenue.

• Develop a deep understanding of what Forrester clients require to be successful as technology executives and leaders.

• Establish an industry presence as an influential speaker and thinker; build relationships with journalists who cover the sector; participate in vendor briefings and field press inquiries as necessary.

• Conduct primary research into 1) architecture strategy, solutions architecture, key technology platforms, and roadmaps, 2) governance and risk management, 3) financial and cost optimization, and 4) performance management including metrics, KPIs, benchmarks etc. Use this research to help clients navigate challenges by providing insights on the future of solutions architecture, cost optimization, investment prioritization, and long-term workplace strategy.

• Conduct deep analysis of IT decision maker challenges and preferences balanced with employee preferences and expectations.

• Create high quality, actionable, analytically deep and fact-based research content throughout the year. Research/write/create approximately 8 to 12 research projects per year, which includes of mix of written reports, tools, webinars, videos, blogs, podcasts, infographics, and other intellectual property. Build visibility for his/her research and contribute to Forrester client communities.

• Drive and lead key Forrester Waves and Landscape reporting for the practice and adjacent areas.

• Consult with clients to apply Forrester’s research in the context of their specific business environment and help solve their problems through inquiry, guidance, and advisory and consulting engagements.

• Present at Forrester-sponsored and industry-related events and deliver client webinars.

• Co-lead the global Forrester Enterprise Architecture forum and award program.

• Contribute to the State of Modern Technology Operations survey, a key adjacent area

• Support business development and prospect conversations as arranged by Forrester’s account leadership teams.
